extracted.intended_audience: clinical trial investigators, protocol authors, journal editors, peer reviewers, and guideline developers involved in designing or reporting randomized and non-standard trials
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and applying SPIRIT and CONSORT extensions for non-standard trial designs, data types, and interventions to ensure complete, transparent reporting of trial protocols and reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply SPIRIT/CONSORT extensions for non-standard trials
rubrics_metrics.description: The main SPIRIT and CONSORT Statements are based on the 'standard' two-group parallel design; many variations (design aspects, interventions, data types) require extension or modification of the main checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the relevant SPIRIT or CONSORT extension when your trial deviates from the standard two-group parallel design (e.g., cluster designs, non-pharmacological interventions, harms data). The listed extensions are intended to improve reporting for these various areas; the list is not exhaustive. If developing a new extension, review the extension policy and register interest via the provided form.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT-C Children & adolescents (SPIRIT 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: SPIRIT extension specifically addressing protocol reporting for trials in children and adolescents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources available: Statement; Explanation & elaboration; Additional materials.
